models.description: Gradient-boosted decision trees optimized for non-linear agro-meteorological tabular features.
strengths: Handles heterogeneous tabular agricultural data without feature scaling
Effectively captures nonlinear interactions between weather, soil texture, and crop coefficients
TreeSHAP gives exact local and global feature attribution (explainability)
Robust to tabular outliers and missing values
limitations: Cannot extrapolate beyond training feature ranges
Does not intrinsically model sequential time series memory
models.suitability_reason: Ideal for single-day point irrigation advisory where complex multi-variable interactions (soil moisture, solar radiation, temperature) determine daily irrigation requirements.

models.description: Deep Multi-Layer Perceptron (128-64-32) capturing continuous microclimatic non-linearities.
strengths: Universal continuous function approximation across multi-dimensional input spaces
Learns smooth transitions between continuous environmental variables (ET0, temperature, humidity)
Extremely low runtime inference latency (< 0.2 ms)
limitations: Requires careful one-hot encoding and min-max feature scaling
Acts as a black box requiring post-hoc sensitivity analysis
Prone to overfitting on small tabular samples without dropout or L2 regularization
models.suitability_reason: Captures smooth continuous non-linear response curves across varying microclimatic and soil water potential gradients.

models.description: Recurrent 2-layer LSTM architecture for sequential and temporal moisture depletion patterns.
strengths: Internal gating mechanisms (input, forget, output gates) retain temporal memory
Captures cumulative soil moisture depletion and multi-day weather trends
Accurately models lagged rainfall effects on subsequent days' irrigation needs
limitations: Higher training and parameter tuning computational cost
Higher inference latency compared to feedforward models
models.suitability_reason: Suitable for continuous sequential scheduling where previous days' drying cycles and cumulative crop water stress dictate current irrigation volume.

external_dataset_validation.dataset_name: Simulated Out-of-Distribution Agronomic Benchmark (ICAR Range Calibrated)
external_dataset_validation.source_url: Calibrated to published ICAR & FAO-56 crop coefficient and regional trial ranges
external_dataset_validation.target_description: Simulated field irrigation depth (mm) across 10 agro-climatic zones designed to test model out-of-distribution generalization
external_dataset_validation.limitations: Programmatically synthesized benchmark dataset; not primary field station IoT sensor telemetry. Designed exclusively for stress-testing out-of-distribution domain shift.
